name: jewish_holidays_and_fasts
title: Jewish Holidays and Fasts
summary: Identify Jewish holidays and fast days for a given Gregorian date, with options for location-based schedules (Israel vs. Diaspora) and Hebrew/English naming conventions.

tools.name: get_holiday_info
tools.description: Get the name of a Jewish holiday or fast day for a specific Gregorian date. This includes all religious holidays and fast days.

params.name: is_israel
params.description: Whether to use the Israel schedule (True) or Diaspora schedule (False).

params.name: hebrew_names
params.description: Whether to return the holiday name in Hebrew characters.

params.name: hebrew_prefix_day
params.description: Whether to prefix multi-day holidays with the day number (e.g., '1 Pesach').

returns.name: holiday_name
returns.description: The name of the holiday or null if no holiday is observed on this date.

returns.name: holiday_display
returns.description: A formatted string containing the holiday name and relevant context if applicable.

returns.name: is_holiday
returns.description: True if the date is a Jewish holiday or fast day.

tools.implementation_notes: 1. Create a GregorianDate instance using GregorianDate(int(date_str[:4]), int(date_str[5:7]), int(date_str[8:10])). 2. Call holiday(greg_date, israel=is_israel, hebrew=hebrew_names, prefix_day=hebrew_prefix_day). 3. Return the results. Note: The library returns None if no holiday is found, library.holiday() returns a None or str. Convert None to null in JSON. 4. If hebrew_names is True, the return value is in Hebrew. If hebrew_names is False, it is transliterated English.

tools.name: get_festival_info
tools.description: Get the name of a Jewish festival for a specific Gregorian date. This excludes fast days and focuses on major and minor religious festivals.

params.name: name_is_hebrew
params.description: Whether to return the festival name in Hebrew characters.

params.name: include_working_days
params.description: Whether to include festival days on which melacha (work) is allowed (e.g., Pesach Sheni, Chol Hamoed).

returns.name: festival_name
returns.description: The name of the festival or null if no holiday is not a festival.

returns.name: festival_display
returns.description: A formatted string containing the festival name.

returns.name: festival_is_festival
returns.description: True if the date is a Jewish festival.

returns.name: festival_is_hebrew
returns.description: True if the name was requested in Hebrew.

tools.implementation_notes: 1. Create a GregorianDate. 2. Call festival(greg_date, israel=is_israel, include_working_days=include_working_days, hebrew=name_is_hebrew, prefix_day=False). 3. Return the results. Note: The library returns None if no festival is found. Convert None to null in agent-facing interface. 4. If name_is_hebrew is True, the return value is in Hebrew.

tools.name: get_today_jewish_date
tools.description: Get the current Jewish (Hebrew) date for today's Gregorian date.

returns.name: hebrew_date_str
returns.description: The current Hebrew date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format (Hebrew year, Hebrew month, Hebrew day).

returns.name: name_is_hebrew
returns.description: True if the date was returned in Hebrew characters.

returns.name: display_date
returns.description: A human-readable string representing the current Hebrew date (e.g., '1 Tishrei 5784').

tools.implementation_notes: 1. Call GregorianDate.today(). 2. Convert the resulting GregorianDate to HebrewDate using .to_heb(). 3. Return the components of thehebrew_date.tuple() and format them into a display string. 4. Note: The library provides a GregorianDate.today() method.

tools.name: get_hebrew_date_from_gregorian
tools.description: Convert a Gregorian date to its corresponding Hebrew date.

params.name: name_is_hebrew
params.description: Whether to return the Hebrew date in Hebrew characters.

returns.name: hebrew_date_tuple
returns.description: The Hebrew date components (year, month, day).

returns.name: conversion_results
returns.description: A human-readable string of the Hebrew date (e.g., '15 Shevat 5783').

tools.implementation_notes: 1. Create a GregorianDate instance from date_str. 2. Call .to_heb() on the GregorianDate instance. 3. Return the components of the HebrewDate.tuple() and a formatted string. 4. Note: The library returns a HebrewDate object.

uncertainties: B.C.E. dates may return inconsistent results when converting between date types.
